# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, but I cannot speak, only gesture to Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak to Blind and me, but Deaf cannot hear anything. Blind can manipulate the bomb and hear speech, but cannot see anything.

Right now, no signs have been agreed upon ("a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). If I send gestures now, Deaf has no context to interpret them and might mistake them for counts, positions, or actions, leading to a fatal mistake. 

Deaf and Blind will speak in their turns this round. Deaf will describe the visual elements of the bomb and establish a signalling protocol (such as thumbs-up/thumbs-down or numbering) for me to direct the defusal. I will wait for Deaf's description and code before sending instructions.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile info: Strip is engraved with three symbols: reversed capital B, upside-down capital T, reversed capital B. Keypad slots: 1 has digit 9, 2 has digit 7, 3 has digit 8, 4 has digit 1. Keypad expects 2 digits, none entered yet. There are 6 wire positions. Display and light are visual-only, so Deaf must describe them.
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY shows 8. LIGHT is yellow. STRIP is painted red, red, blue. KEYPAD has buttons 1: 9, 2: 7, 3: 8, 4: 1, requires 2 digits, entered nothing. WIRES are 1: red, 2: orange, 3: yellow, 4: green, 5: white, 6: blue. Mute, check manual and gesture to me what Blind must do.

I have reviewed the defusal manual against the bomb details provided by Deaf and Blind:

Manual instructions:
1. Cut the green wire.
2. Press the key that wears 9.
3. Cut the blue wire.
4. Press the key that wears 1.
"In that order, and in no other."

Deaf identified the wires:
1: red, 2: orange, 3: yellow, 4: green, 5: white, 6: blue.
Therefore, Step 1 is cutting wire 4 (green).

To avoid any ambiguity or order confusion, I will direct the defusal one step at a time. I am signalling Step 1 to Deaf using scissors (✌) followed by four index fingers (☝ ☝ ☝ ☝) to indicate cutting wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute signaled cut wire 4. Cut the fourth wire (wire 4). Current bomb status: DISPLAY is now 3, LIGHT is now red. Mute: after wire 4 is cut, gesture the next instruction. Use ✌ [count] for wires, 🫵 [digit buttons] for keypad.

Deaf explicitly instructed: "after wire 4 is cut, gesture the next instruction."

Because of the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf), Blind has not yet taken their turn to hear Deaf's instruction and cut wire 4. The manual strictly states: "In that order, and in no other." Signaling the next action before wire 4 has been confirmed cut risks having actions executed out of order, which would detonate the bomb.

I will wait for Blind to cut wire 4 and for Deaf to confirm it before signaling the next step.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: Cutting wire 4 now.
Deaf says: Wire 4 was cut successfully! Current state: DISPLAY is 6. LIGHT is red. STRIP is red, red, blue. KEYPAD buttons: 1 is 9, 2 is 7, 3 is 8, 4 is 1. WIRES remaining: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 5 white, 6 blue. Mute, please gesture what to do next!

To follow the manual's exact sequence ("press the key that wears 9"), the next step is pressing Keypad Button 1 (which has digit 9). 

Following Deaf's established convention (`🫵 [digit buttons] for keypad`), I will signal `🫵` followed by a single `☝` to indicate button 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute signaled 🫵 ☝. Blind: press button 1 on the keypad (position 1, label 9). Current bomb status: DISPLAY is 1. LIGHT is yellow. STRIP is red, red, blue.

Deaf has relayed the instruction to Blind to press button 1. Blind has not acted yet, as the turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. 

The manual strictly requires executing each step in exact sequence. I must wait for Blind to press key 1 (digit 9) and for Deaf to confirm before signaling the third step (cut the blue wire, wire 6).

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: key accepted, 1 digits to go
Blind says to Mute: Pressed slot 1 (digit 9) on the keypad.
Deaf says: Key 9 accepted! Keypad has [entered 9], 1 digit to go. Current bomb status: DISPLAY is now 2. LIGHT is yellow. STRIP is red, red, blue. KEYPAD buttons: 1:[9], 2:[7], 3:[8], 4:[1]. Mute, please gesture the next action!

I need Deaf to tell Blind to cut the blue wire, which is wire 6.

Following the established convention (`✌ [count] for wires`), I will send `✌` followed by six `☝` to denote wire 6.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute signaled cut wire 6 (✌ with six counts). Blind: cut wire 6! Current bomb status: DISPLAY is 1. LIGHT is blue. STRIP is red, red, blue. KEYPAD has entered 9.

Deaf has relayed the command to Blind to cut wire 6. Blind has not cut it yet because Blind acts after Mute in the turn order.

I must wait for Blind to cut wire 6 and for Deaf to confirm before giving the fourth and final instruction ("press the key that wears 1").

```
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: all required wires are cut
Blind says to Mute: Cutting wire 6 now.
Deaf says: All required wires are cut! Only the keypad remains: entered [9], 1 digit left to complete. DISPLAY is 9. LIGHT is blue. STRIP is red, red, blue. KEYPAD buttons: 1:[9], 2:[7], 3:[8], 4:[1]. Mute, gesture the next keypad button!

The final instruction from the manual is: "then press the key that wears 1."
Button 4 wears the digit 1.
Using the keypad gesture convention established by Deaf (`🫵 [digit buttons]`), I will gesture `🫵` followed by four `☝` symbols to indicate button 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Mute signaled button 4 (🫵 with 4 counts). Blind: press button 4 on the keypad (position 4, label 1) to finish defusing!

I have relayed all instructions from the manual. Blind will now press button 4 to complete the defusal sequence. I will wait.

```
wait()
```
